<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

payload.prompt:
Build a Python static-analysis stack for Java-like programs in `/workspace`.
The repository already contains the shared program model, utilities,
benchmarks, and `run.sh`; extend that base through three dependent layers:

`soot_analysis.py`
Build the Jimple-like IR and the core whole-program analysis utilities,
including CHA call-graph construction, the scene registry, copy propagation,
and dead-code elimination.

`flowdroid_analysis.py`
Add the FlowDroid-style IFDS taint analysis on top of that IR and call graph,
including access paths, taint facts, alias support, source/sink handling, and
lifecycle-aware propagation.

`stubdroid_analysis.py`
Finish with automatic library-summary generation plus the summary-aware taint
wrapper and analysis layer.

Each module should still run standalone via `python3 <module>.py`, and
`run.sh` must execute all three layers with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` while emitting
the required `KEY: VALUE` experiment lines. Use `requirements/` as the source
of truth for the detailed contracts.



You are running as a long-horizon autonomous engineering agent at
`/workspace`. This task spans many files and requirements, and is expected
to take many iterations.

Read every requirement under `/workspace/requirements/` (and any other
explicit requirement list referenced by the task) and only finish once
every single one is addressed. Cherry-picking or partial fixes will lead
to failure.

If you believe the task is complex enough to benefit from a plan, you may
write `/workspace/agent_plans/plan.json` before making changes. This is
optional. If you create it, it must be a JSON object with `nodes` and
`edges`. Each node must have string `id` equal to a requirement slug from
`/workspace/requirements/`, may include `label` and `layer`, and each edge
must use string `from` and `to` that reference those ids.

`/workspace` is initialized as a git repo. After finishing the
implementation for ONE requirement:

  1. `cd /workspace`
  2. `git add -A`
  3. `git diff --cached > requirement_patches/<slug>.diff`
  4. `git commit -m "impl: <slug>"`

Where `<slug>` is the requirement filename without the `.yaml` extension.
The patch file MUST be non-empty for the requirement to count as complete.

prior work has done — only your own commits will be there; no reference
solution is accessible.

12	Public API (stable — other layers import these names):
13	
14	- `class Scene(program: Program)`
15	  - attrs: `program`, `classes: dict[str, ClassDef]`, `methods: dict[str, tuple[ClassDef, Method]]` (keyed by full signature), `hierarchy: dict[str, list[str]]`

18	  - `resolve_method(class_name, method_name, param_types) -> tuple[ClassDef, Method] | None` — walks superclasses, matches by name + arity

26	  - `reachable_methods() -> set[str]`, `callees_from(sig) -> set[str]`, `num_edges() -> int`
27	- `build_cha_call_graph(scene: Scene, entry_points=None) -> CallGraph` — CHA: virtual calls target the declared class method plus overrides in all subclasses.
28	- `copy_propagate(statements: list[Statement]) -> tuple[list[Statement], int]`
29	- `eliminate_dead_code(statements: list[Statement]) -> tuple[list[Statement], int]`
30	- `analyze_benchmark(path: str) -> dict` (stats)
31	- `main(argv)` — prints per benchmark: `LAYER: soot`, `BENCHMARK: <name>`, `CLASSES: n`, `METHODS: n`,

35	
36	Imports from `soot_analysis`: `Scene`, `CallGraph`, `build_cha_call_graph`, `build_cfg`, `CFG`.
37	Imports from `program_model`: everything needed. MUST NOT modify other files.
38	
39	Public API:
40	
41	- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class AccessPath` — `base: str`, `fields: tuple[str, ...] = ()`;
42	  `__str__` renders `base.f1.f2`; `extend(field: str) -> AccessPath`.
43	- `@dataclass class TaintFact` — `access_path: AccessPath`, `source_stmt: int`, `source_method: str`,
44	  `category: str`, `path: tuple[str, ...]` (human-readable trace, e.g. `("r3", "r4.secret", "r5")`).
45	- `@dataclass class Leak` — `source_stmt: int`, `sink_stmt: int`, `source_method: str`, `sink_method: str`,
46	  `source_category: str`, `sink_category: str`, `tainted_path: list[str]`,
47	  `source_method_sig: str`, `sink_method_sig: str` (full signatures of the methods CONTAINING source/sink statements).
48	- `class IFDSTaintAnalysis`
49	  - `__init__(self, program: Program, scene: Scene | None = None, call_graph: CallGraph | None = None,
50	    summaries: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] | None = None)`
51	  - `run(self) -> list[Leak]`; after run: `.leaks`, `.facts_count: int`
52	  - `summaries` maps a callee FULL SIGNATURE to flows `(src, dst)` where src/dst are strings:
53	    `"parameterI"` (0-based), `"this"`, `"this.<field>"`, `"return"`. When a call target has a summary,
54	    apply the flows at the call site and DO NOT descend into the callee body or apply default rules.
55	- `analyze_program(program, summaries=None) -> list[Leak]`
56	- `match_leaks(detected: list[Leak], expected: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, float, float]` —
57	  an expected leak is matched when a detected leak has the same `source_method` and `sink_method`;
58	  returns (num_matched_expected, precision, recall).
59	
60	Semantics (must pass all benchmarks under `benchmarks/`):
61	
62	- Forward, flow-sensitive IFDS-style taint over each method's CFG, fixpoint per method; interprocedural via
63	  CHA call graph with global fixpoint iteration over reachable methods (context-insensitive is OK).
64	- Source statements (`stmt.is_source`, or callee matches `program.source_sink_spec["sources"]` by class+method name):
65	  taint `stmt.lhs` with category. Sink statements (`stmt.is_sink` or spec match): if any arg or the receiver is
66	  tainted, record a `Leak` carrying the taint path.
67	- `assign`: propagate taint rhs->lhs (kill lhs when rhs is untainted constant). `new`: lhs fresh/untainted.
68	- Field taint store is GLOBAL and keyed by `(declaring_class, field_name)` (field-sensitive, object-insensitive):
69	  `field_store base.f = v` taints/kills that key; `field_load lhs = base.f` reads it. This gives cross-method
70	  lifecycle propagation (benchmark 05) and alias loads (benchmark 04) for free, but ALSO implement explicit
71	  alias tracking: `assign a = b` on reference types records a may-alias b; a store through one alias must be
72	  visible to loads through the other (the global field store already ensures this; keep alias sets for reporting).
73	- Calls to methods WITH bodies: map tainted args -> callee `param_locals[i]`, tainted receiver -> callee
74	  `this_local`; callee return taint maps back to `stmt.lhs`. Global field store is shared, so callee field
75	  effects are visible at the caller. Iterate all reachable methods to a global fixpoint.
76	- Calls to library methods WITHOUT bodies and WITHOUT summaries (e.g. `StringBuilder.append`): default rule —
77	  if any arg or the receiver is tainted, taint `stmt.lhs` (when present) and the receiver. Never apply the
78	  default rule to source/sink statements.
79	- Lifecycle-aware: every entry point in `program.entry_points` is analyzed; tainted component fields persist
80	  across entry points via the global field store (onCreate -> onResume in benchmark 05).
81	- Verification: compare against `program.expected_leaks` via `match_leaks`.
82	
83	Standalone output per benchmark: `LAYER: flowdroid`, `BENCHMARK: <name>`, `SOURCES: n`, `SINKS: n`,
84	`TAINT_FACTS: n`, `EXPECTED_LEAKS: n`, `DETECTED_LEAKS: n`, one `LEAK: source=<src_method>:<stmt> sink=<sink_method>:<stmt> path=<p1 -> p2 ...>` per detected leak,
85	`PRECISION: <0..1>`, `RECALL: <0..1>`, `STATUS: PASS|FAIL` (PASS iff recall == 1.0 and precision == 1.0).
86	Final line: `OVERALL: PASS|FAIL`. Exit code always 0.
87	
88	Expected results on benchmarks: 01..06 each exactly 1 leak detected & matched; 07 zero leaks, STATUS PASS.
89	
90	## Layer 3: stubdroid_analysis.py
91	
92	Imports from `soot_analysis` (`Scene`, `build_cha_call_graph`) and `flowdroid_analysis`
93	(`IFDSTaintAnalysis`, `Leak`, `TaintFact`, `AccessPath`, `analyze_program`, `match_leaks`).
94	MUST NOT modify other files.
95	
96	Public API:
97	
98	- `@dataclass class SummaryFlow` — `source: str`, `target: str` (same descriptor strings as the contract above).
99	- `@dataclass class MethodSummary` — `signature: str` (full sig), `class_name: str`, `method_name: str`,
100	  `flows: list[SummaryFlow]`, `from_metadata: bool`.
101	- `class SummaryGenerator`
102	  - `__init__(self, scene: Scene)`
103	  - `generate(self) -> dict[str, MethodSummary]` — one summary per method of every library class
104	    (`ClassDef.is_library`) that has a body and at least one flow.
105	  - If a statement carries `metadata["summary_flow"]` (e.g. `"parameter0 -> this._elements"`), use it directly
106	    (`from_metadata=True`). Otherwise derive flows by symbolic intraprocedural propagation: tag each param as
107	    `parameterI` and `this` fields as `this.<field>`; propagate through `assign`/`field_load`/`field_store`;
108	    a tag reaching a `return` rhs produces target `return`; a tag stored into a `this` field produces
109	    `this.<field>`. Merge flows per method; ignore pure `identity`/`nop` statements beyond seeding tags.
110	- `summaries_to_dict(summaries: dict[str, MethodSummary]) -> dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]]` — adapter for
111	  `IFDSTaintAnalysis`.
112	- `class SummaryAwareTaintAnalysis` — thin wrapper that builds a Scene + CHA call graph, generates summaries,
113	  and runs `IFDSTaintAnalysis(program, scene, call_graph, summaries=...)`; `.run() -> list[Leak]`,
114	  exposes `.summaries`.
115	- `analyze_program_with_summaries(program) -> tuple[list[Leak], dict[str, MethodSummary]]`
116	
117	Standalone main: for each benchmark, generate summaries and run the summary-aware analysis. Print per
118	benchmark: `LAYER: stubdroid`, `BENCHMARK: <name>`, `SUMMARIES_GENERATED: n`,
119	`SUMMARY: <full_sig> :: <src -> dst; ...>` per summary, then `EXPECTED_LEAKS: n`, `DETECTED_LEAKS: n`,
120	`LEAK: ...` lines, `PRECISION:`, `RECALL:`, `STATUS: PASS|FAIL`. Final `OVERALL: PASS|FAIL`. Exit code 0.
